questions.q: The line `geozone 1 0 0 0 8000 0 2 2`. What kind of zone is it?
options: A polygon, a fly zone, from the ground to 80 m, action RTH
A circle, a no-fly zone, from the ground to 80 m, action POS_HOLD
A circle, a fly zone, from the ground to 8000 m, action AVOID
A polygon, a no-fly zone, from 80 m with no ceiling, POS_HOLD
questions.explain: The fields in order: id 1, shape 0 — circular, type 0 — exclusive (NFZ), min 0, max 8000 cm = 80 m, altitudes relative to home, action 2 — POS_HOLD, two vertices (center and radius).

questions.q: A circular zone has `geozone vertex 1 1 12000 0`. What does 12000 mean?
options: The latitude 0.0012000° of a second point on the circumference of the zone
The zone ceiling altitude: 12000 cm above the home point
A radius of 120 m: for a circle vertex 1 holds centimeters
The detection distance of this particular zone: 120 m
questions.explain: In `geoZoneInit()` for a circle the `lat` value of the vertex with index 1 is taken as the radius in centimeters; `lon` is not used. The center is vertex 0.

questions.q: An NFZ is defined with `min alt = 3000`, `max alt = 0`. The aircraft is on the ground inside its outline. What about arming?
options: Arming is forbidden: the aircraft is inside the outline of a no-fly zone
Arming is allowed: at altitude 0 the aircraft is outside the altitude range of the zone
Arming is allowed only with an emergency arm that overrides the blocks
Arming is forbidden until `geozone_safehome_as_inclusive` is enabled
questions.explain: After the outline check `isInGeozone()` checks the altitude: z ≥ min (if min is not 0) and z ≤ max. On the ground z = 0 is less than 30 m, so the aircraft is not in the zone and `geozoneIsBlockingArming()` does not take it into account.

questions.q: In the config a zone has `vertex count = 4`, but there are three `geozone vertex` lines for it. What happens after a reboot?
options: The zone becomes a triangle of three vertices
Only this zone is disabled, the others work
Arming is blocked by the GEOZONE flag
The geozone task is turned off entirely and silently
questions.explain: `geoZoneInit()` compares the sum of `vertex count` with the number of stored vertices; on a mismatch it turns TASK_GEOZONE off. After that there is no arming block, no actions and no detour in RTH.

questions.q: In which set of modes do geozones execute actions (AVOID, POS_HOLD, RTH)?
options: ANGLE, HORIZON, NAV CRUISE, NAV COURSE HOLD
In all except MANUAL
Only in NAV POSHOLD and NAV RTH
ACRO, ANGLE and NAV WP
questions.explain: `isNonGeozoneModeFromBoxInput()` returns “not a geozone mode” if none of the four is active: ANGLE, HORIZON, NAV CRUISE, NAV COURSE HOLD. In ACRO and MANUAL INAV does not intervene.

questions.q: RTH with active geozones found no detour, `geozone_no_way_home_action` is at the default. What does the aircraft do?
options: Hovers or loiters until the pilot gives a command
Performs an emergency landing on the spot
Flies home in a straight line, ignoring the zones
Returns along the recorded trackback points
questions.explain: The default is RTH: an ordinary straight-line return through the zones. The value EMRG_LAND gives an emergency landing. The choice has to be made deliberately for the terrain.

questions.q: Armed 172 m from safehome 3 and 176 m from safehome 1, both enabled; safehome 2 is 71 m away but disabled. `safehome_max_distance = 20000`. Which one is selected?
options: Safehome 2: it is the closest of all to the arming point
Safehome 1: the lower index of the two suitable ones
Safehome 3: the nearest enabled one within 200 m
None: two close candidates are ambiguous
questions.explain: `findNearestSafeHome()` skips disabled entries and takes the nearest of the rest if the distance is no more than `safehome_max_distance`. The index order does not matter.

questions.q: `nav_rth_trackback_distance = 500`. What units is this value in, and what is it measured from?
options: Centimeters of path traveled along the recorded track
Meters in a straight line from the place where the trackback started
Meters in a straight line from the home point to the aircraft
Seconds of flight along the recorded track before RTH
questions.explain: The setting is in meters (50–2000). `rthTrackBackSetNewPosition()` compares it with the straight-line distance from the last saved point — the place where the trackback started; when it is exceeded, a normal RTH takes over.

questions.q: `fwapproach 3 5000 0 1 270 -180 0`. With which headings can INAV land the wing?
options: Only 270° and 180°
Only 90° and 360°
questions.explain: A positive heading also allows the opposite direction: 270° and 90°. A negative one — only the heading itself: 180°. A heading of 0 would mean “disabled”.

questions.q: approach alt = 5000, `nav_fw_land_approach_length = 40000`, land alt = 0. What is the altitude of `WP_FINAL_APPROACH`, and where is the target of the final leg?
options: 33.32 m; the target is 400 m beyond the landing point at an altitude of −33.32 m
33.33 m; the target is at the landing point itself at an altitude of 0 m, with no margin
50 m; the target is 400 m before the landing point at an altitude of 33.32 m
25 m; the target is 200 m beyond the landing point at an altitude of 0 m above it
questions.explain: h_fa = 5000 / 3 × 2 in integers = 3332 cm. `WP_LAND` is moved by L forward along the landing heading and lowered to land alt − h_fa, so the target line meets the ground before the landing point.
